enterprises.name: Alderbrook
enterprises.description: A B2B SaaS company of about 85 people selling spend and expense management to mid-market finance teams. Founded 2019, mid-way through moving off its original self-managed infrastructure.
enterprises.goal: Grow recurring revenue without growing the platform team, while keeping SOC 2 and GDPR commitments intact.

businessCapabilities.name: Product Management
businessCapabilities.description: Deciding what to build and what to decline.

businessCapabilities.name: Software Engineering
businessCapabilities.description: Designing, building and reviewing the product.

businessCapabilities.name: Platform Operations
businessCapabilities.description: Keeping the runtime available and the delivery pipeline fast.

businessCapabilities.name: Security & Compliance
businessCapabilities.description: SOC 2, GDPR, customer security reviews, vulnerability response.

businessCapabilities.name: Data & Analytics
businessCapabilities.description: Turning product and commercial events into decisions.

businessCapabilities.name: Demand Generation
businessCapabilities.description: Creating qualified interest in the product.

businessCapabilities.name: Customer Onboarding
businessCapabilities.description: Getting a signed customer to routine daily use.

businessCapabilities.name: Customer Support
businessCapabilities.description: Answering, diagnosing and escalating customer issues.

businessCapabilities.name: Incident Management
businessCapabilities.description: Detecting, mitigating and learning from production incidents.

businessCapabilities.name: Subscription Billing
businessCapabilities.description: Turning a contract into an invoice and a payment, every month.

businessCapabilities.name: Revenue Recognition
businessCapabilities.description: Recognising subscription revenue over the contract term.

businessCapabilities.name: On-Premise Delivery
businessCapabilities.description: Installing and supporting the product inside a customer’s own data centre. Three accounts remain, all contracted to move to the hosted product by the end of 2026.

businessProcesses.name: Production incident response
businessProcesses.description: What happens between an alert firing and the incident being closed. Modelled because the hand-off between the on-call engineer and customer support was the part that kept going wrong.
businessProcesses.triggerEvent: A monitor breaches its threshold and pages the on-call engineer.
businessProcesses.outcome: Service restored, customers informed, and a review recorded with at least one action.

businessProcesses.name: New customer workspace setup
businessProcesses.description: From countersigned contract to the customer’s first approved expense. The step that dominates the elapsed time is the accounting-ledger connection, which is why the integrations squad owns half of it.
businessProcesses.outcome: Workspace live, policy configured, ledger connected, first expense approved.

businessProcesses.name: Monthly invoice run
businessProcesses.description: Runs on the second working day of each month. Currently executes twice — once in the in-house billing service and once in Stripe Billing — while accounts are migrated across.
businessProcesses.triggerEvent: Second working day of the month.
businessProcesses.outcome: Every active subscription invoiced once, and the ledger reconciled.

valueStreams.name: Trial to paying customer
valueStreams.description: From a finance lead first hearing the name to their team filing expenses in it every week.

valueStreams.name: Idea to released feature
valueStreams.description: From a problem worth solving to the change being measurable in production.

valueStreams.name: Incident to resolution
valueStreams.description: From the first signal that something is wrong to the change that stops it recurring.

architectureDomains.name: Business Architecture
architectureDomains.description: Capabilities, value streams and the processes that run the company.

architectureDomains.name: Data Architecture
architectureDomains.description: The information Alderbrook holds, where it lives and how it moves.

architectureDomains.name: Application Architecture
architectureDomains.description: The product itself and the systems the company is run on.

architectureDomains.name: Technology Architecture
architectureDomains.description: Compute, storage, networking and the tooling that delivers them.

architectureDomains.name: Security Architecture
architectureDomains.description: Added by Alderbrook rather than seeded: SOC 2 made security a review lens of its own, so anything a customer auditor asks about carries this domain too.

organizationUnits.name: Engineering
organizationUnits.description: Builds and runs the product. Four teams, 38 people.

organizationUnits.name: Platform Team
organizationUnits.description: Owns runtime, delivery pipeline and observability for every other squad.

organizationUnits.name: Core Product Squad
organizationUnits.description: Expense capture, policy and approvals — the surface most customers touch daily.

organizationUnits.name: Integrations Squad
organizationUnits.description: Card networks, accounting ledgers and the public API.

organizationUnits.name: Security & Compliance
organizationUnits.description: Two people carrying SOC 2, GDPR and customer security reviews.

organizationUnits.name: Go to Market
organizationUnits.description: Everything from first touch to renewal. 31 people.

organizationUnits.name: Customer Success
organizationUnits.description: Onboarding and ongoing account health; also fields tier-2 support.

organizationUnits.name: General & Administrative
organizationUnits.description: Finance, people and the internal tooling they run on. 16 people.

buildingBlocks.name: Product Platform
buildingBlocks.description: Everything Alderbrook sells. The boundary that decides whether a change is product work or internal work.

buildingBlocks.name: Corporate Systems
buildingBlocks.description: Everything Alderbrook is run on but does not sell.

buildingBlocks.name: Revenue Systems
buildingBlocks.description: The chain from a signed contract to recognised revenue. Currently the least settled segment in the landscape.

buildingBlocks.name: Engineering Platform
buildingBlocks.description: The runtime, pipeline and observability every squad builds on. Owned by one team of six.

buildingBlocks.name: Data Platform
buildingBlocks.description: Where product and commercial events are collected, modelled and read.

buildingBlocks.name: Workplace Systems
buildingBlocks.description: Mail, chat, documents, HR. Bought, never built.

buildingBlocks.name: Identity & Access Management
buildingBlocks.description: One account per person, one sign-in, and a record of who can reach what. Serves both the product and the company.

buildingBlocks.name: Expense Capture
buildingBlocks.description: Getting a receipt off a phone and into a structured expense without anyone typing an amount twice.

buildingBlocks.name: Policy & Approval
buildingBlocks.description: Deciding whether a given spend is allowed, and routing it to whoever must say so.

buildingBlocks.name: Card Issuing
buildingBlocks.description: Issuing virtual and physical cards with the policy already applied at the point of spend.

buildingBlocks.name: Ledger Integration
buildingBlocks.description: Pushing approved spend into whatever accounting system the customer already runs. The single largest source of onboarding delay.

buildingBlocks.name: Subscription Billing
buildingBlocks.description: Turning contracts into invoices and payments. Mid-replacement: built in-house in 2020, moving to a bought service through 2026.

buildingBlocks.name: Customer Relationship Management
buildingBlocks.description: One record of every account, from first touch to renewal.

buildingBlocks.name: Support Desk
buildingBlocks.description: Receiving, tracking and answering customer issues.

buildingBlocks.name: Analytics Warehouse
buildingBlocks.description: The one place where a product question and a commercial question can be answered with the same numbers.

buildingBlocks.name: Observability
buildingBlocks.description: Knowing that something is wrong before a customer tells you.

buildingBlocks.name: Continuous Delivery
buildingBlocks.description: Getting a merged change into production without a person in the path.

buildingBlocks.name: Application Runtime
buildingBlocks.description: Where the product’s services actually execute. Being replaced wholesale: self-managed VMs out, managed Kubernetes in.

buildingBlocks.name: Relational Data Store
buildingBlocks.description: Durable transactional storage for the product.

buildingBlocks.name: Object Storage
buildingBlocks.description: Receipt images and exports. Cheap, large, and subject to the longest retention obligations in the estate.

buildingBlocks.name: Secrets Management
buildingBlocks.description: Issuing and rotating credentials without them landing in a repository.

buildingBlocks.name: HR Information
buildingBlocks.description: The authoritative list of who works here, which is also what joiner-mover-leaver access depends on.

buildingBlocks.name: Alderbrook Web App
buildingBlocks.description: React SPA. The surface finance teams live in.

buildingBlocks.name: Alderbrook Mobile App
buildingBlocks.description: Where receipts are actually captured. Two thirds of expenses start here.

buildingBlocks.name: Public API Gateway
buildingBlocks.description: The documented, versioned entry point for customer integrations.

buildingBlocks.name: Expense Monolith
buildingBlocks.description: The original Rails application. Still owns policy evaluation and the approval queue; everything else has been carved out of it.

buildingBlocks.name: Receipt OCR Service
buildingBlocks.description: Extracts merchant, amount, date and tax from an image. The one service whose failures customers notice within minutes.

buildingBlocks.name: Policy Service
buildingBlocks.description: Carves policy evaluation out of the monolith. Designed, not yet built — the last big piece before the monolith can be switched off.

buildingBlocks.name: Card Service
buildingBlocks.description: Talks to the card issuing processor and applies policy at authorisation time.

buildingBlocks.name: Ledger Connector Service
buildingBlocks.description: One adapter per accounting system. Nine supported, three of which cover 80% of accounts.

buildingBlocks.name: Notification Service
buildingBlocks.description: Email, push and in-app. Shared by product and by billing.

buildingBlocks.name: Auth0
buildingBlocks.description: Original identity provider. Replaced when per-active-user pricing overtook the cost of running Keycloak.

buildingBlocks.name: Keycloak
buildingBlocks.description: Self-hosted identity provider. Carries customer SSO, which is now a standard requirement in mid-market deals.

buildingBlocks.name: HashiCorp Vault
buildingBlocks.description: Dynamic database credentials and certificate issuance.

buildingBlocks.name: In-House Billing Service
buildingBlocks.description: Written in a fortnight in 2020 and load-bearing ever since. Being retired account by account; roughly a third of revenue still invoices through it.

buildingBlocks.name: Stripe Billing
buildingBlocks.description: Bought replacement. Live for new accounts since June 2026; migration of existing accounts runs to Q1 2027.

buildingBlocks.name: NetSuite
buildingBlocks.description: General ledger and revenue recognition.

buildingBlocks.name: HubSpot
buildingBlocks.description: CRM and marketing automation on one record.

buildingBlocks.name: Zendesk
buildingBlocks.description: Customer-facing ticketing.

buildingBlocks.name: Personio
buildingBlocks.description: HR system of record. Joiner-mover-leaver events here drive access provisioning in Keycloak.

buildingBlocks.name: Google Workspace
buildingBlocks.description: Mail, calendar, documents.

buildingBlocks.name: Slack
buildingBlocks.description: Also where incident channels are opened, which makes it load-bearing during an outage.

buildingBlocks.name: Postgres (product primary)
buildingBlocks.description: Managed Postgres. Single primary with a read replica; the read replica is what analytics extracts from.

buildingBlocks.name: Redis
buildingBlocks.description: Session cache and the approval job queue.

buildingBlocks.name: S3 Receipt Store
buildingBlocks.description: Receipt images, seven-year retention. The bucket a customer auditor always asks about.

buildingBlocks.name: Segment
buildingBlocks.description: Collects product events once and fans them out to the warehouse and to marketing.

buildingBlocks.name: Snowflake
buildingBlocks.description: The warehouse. Product events, subscription data and CRM records land here.

buildingBlocks.name: dbt
buildingBlocks.description: Transformations and the tests that stop a broken model reaching a dashboard.

buildingBlocks.name: Metabase
buildingBlocks.description: Self-service dashboards. Where a commercial question gets answered without asking an engineer.

buildingBlocks.name: Self-Managed VM Fleet
buildingBlocks.description: The original infrastructure: EC2 instances configured by hand, later by Terraform. Contracted to be switched off at the end of 2026 — the remaining question is what is still on it.

buildingBlocks.name: Managed Kubernetes Cluster
buildingBlocks.description: The replacement runtime. Everything except the monolith and the in-house billing service now runs here.

buildingBlocks.name: AWS Production Account
buildingBlocks.description: The account everything customer-facing lives in. Separate accounts exist for staging and for the data platform.

buildingBlocks.name: Terraform
buildingBlocks.description: Infrastructure as code. Covers the Kubernetes cluster completely and the VM fleet only partly, which is itself a reason to retire the fleet.

buildingBlocks.name: GitHub Actions
buildingBlocks.description: Build, test and deploy. Replaced a self-hosted Jenkins in 2020.

buildingBlocks.name: Datadog
buildingBlocks.description: Metrics, logs and traces.

buildingBlocks.name: PagerDuty
buildingBlocks.description: On-call rotation and escalation.

buildingBlocks.name: Public Status Page
buildingBlocks.description: Customer-facing incident communication. Deliberately hosted outside the production account.

buildingBlocks.name: On-Premise Installer
buildingBlocks.description: Packaged the product for three enterprise customers’ own data centres. No longer sold; the last contract ends with 2026.
